reviewer: Independent Sol review and root integration
scope: Local v3 release-origin publisher incident. Real loopback HTTP and Go handlers, PostgreSQL 17.11 with migration 001 and restricted runtime role. Synthetic development publisher bearer and ephemeral Ed25519 fixture keys.

tools.go: go1.27.1 darwin/arm64 (PostgreSQL runs and root verification)
tools.execution: Go race-enabled tests on macOS over IPv4 loopback, database reachable only through a private Unix socket

observations.beforeRestart: The initial publication returned 200 and the GET contained the expected signed assignment at sequence 1.
observations.afterRestartSetup: A fresh HTTP listener on the same database used a config with the old publisher bearer removed, the old assignment root revoked, and new values installed.
observations.baseline: The stale sequence-1 offer returned HTTP 200 while the revoked bearer returned 401 and the replacement bearer with a freshly signed old-key sequence-2 write got 409. The failed writes kept the audit body unchanged. Clean sequence-2 publication succeeded and the artifact bytes were unchanged.
observations.candidate: Existing assignment key authorization and Ed25519 verification run on v3 offer reads. The stale offer returned empty HTTP 204. Both write denials, exact audit readback, sequence-2 recovery and original artifact bytes passed again. All wire responses had Cache-Control: no-store.
observations.fixtureLimitation: Synthetic fieldlog-scope v3 metadata with a small signed payload; no installed binary or app-side verifier was invoked.

initialGoSuite.reason: The isolated services-only snapshot omitted the cross-language release-v2 contract fixture.

remaining: Independent review and adoption of the v3 assignment-delivery correction. The pinned baseline still served the revoked offer in the control.

Publisher-compromise coverage here is assignment-key and bearer containment at the origin. Standalone artifact-signing-key compromise, legacy offers, offline trust refresh and already activated clients receive no new evidence.

The release-origin Cache-Control evidence and existing DB/RLS coverage leave any active shared delivery cache and cache freshness unqualified. Inventory the local topology before requiring provider cache tests.

Existing Go tests establish bounded release-route concurrency and payload limits. No integrated local workload receipt was identified with concurrent Phoenix/Oban build work and release delivery, including queue drain and data integrity.
No executed local incident diagnostic/alert and incident/security runbook receipt was identified for G31.

Section 22.2 outage evidence is partial. The iOS replay reopened without a delivery URL, and the Android replay used bundled releases. No receipt was identified for the app remaining useful during failures of the active control-plane/delivery and telemetry paths. Billing remains disabled for free use.
Separate owner lanes retain new signer integration and live compiler cancellation.
gateRecommendation: Keep L07 open. Review the private candidate as a bounded G30 v3 origin-containment slice and attach the verified existing receipts at their actual scope.
